text: Take I-90 to Exit 52 (Snoqualmie Pass West) and turn left under the freeway onto Alpental Road. In about 0.1 mile take the first right, signed for the parking pass, and in another 0.1 mile keep right for the main Pacific Crest Trail North lot, around 3,000 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required.

pins.name: PCT North Trailhead, Snoqualmie Pass (I-90 Exit 52)

text: Take I-90 to Exit 52 at Snoqualmie Pass. Cross under the freeway and take the first right; the PCT North (Commonwealth Basin) trailhead lot is a large paved lot on the right, at about 3,000 feet. Self-issue a Northwest Forest Pass ($5) at the trailhead before heading north on the Pacific Crest Trail into the Alpine Lakes Wilderness.

pins.name: PCT North / Snoqualmie Pass North Trailhead
PCT Trailhead, Snoqualmie Pass (Exit 52, Alpental Rd)

text: From I-90 Exit 52 (Snoqualmie Pass West), head north under the freeway onto Alpental Road and take the first right after about 0.1 mile, signed for a parking pass; the main Pacific Crest Trail North trailhead lot is to the right where the road splits. A Northwest Forest Pass or interagency pass is required to park, and a free self-issued Alpine Lakes Wilderness permit is filled out at the kiosk.

From I-90 Exit 52 (Snoqualmie Pass West), head north under the freeway onto Alpental Road and take the first right after about 0.1 mile, signed for a parking pass; the main Pacific Crest Trail North trailhead lot is to the right where the road splits. A Northwest Forest Pass or interagency pass is required to park, and a free self-issued Alpine Lakes Wilderness permit is filled out at the kiosk.

This scramble starts at the Pacific Crest Trailhead at Snoqualmie Pass West, reached via I-90 Exit 52 — the road-access endpoint for the hike. The lot sits at about 3,000 feet, and parking here fills on weekends, so get an early start on busy days.

pins.name: PCT Northbound Trailhead (Kendall Peak / Kendall Katwalk access)

text: Leave I-90 at Exit 52 (Snoqualmie Pass West), go north under the freeway onto Alpental Road, and in about 0.1 mile turn right onto the dirt spur into the PCT North Trailhead lot at about 3,000 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass or interagency pass is required to park, and the roughly 50-car lot fills early on weekends; self-issue the free wilderness permit at the trailhead.

From I-90 Exit 52 at Snoqualmie Pass, go north under the freeway onto Alpental Road and after 0.1 mile turn right at the Forest Service sign into the Pacific Crest Trail North trailhead lots, at about 3,000 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park.

From I-90 Exit 80 (Roslyn/Salmon la Sac), go north on Bullfrog Road 2.8 miles through two roundabouts and continue on SR 903 through Roslyn and past Cle Elum Lake to Forest Road 46, about 16.8 miles from the freeway. Turn left (west) on FR 46 for 4.7 miles, then right on FR 4616 for about 1 mile to the Pete Lake trailhead at about 2,800 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass and a self-issued wilderness perm
Reached on FR-4616 off Cooper Lake Road, past Cooper Lake.

From I-90 Exit 80, go north on Bullfrog Road through two traffic circles onto SR 903, then follow SR 903 through Roslyn and past Cle Elum Lake to Cooper Lake Road (FR 46), about 16.8 miles from the freeway. Turn left on FR 46 for 4.7 miles, then right on FR 4616 for about 1 mile to the Pete Lake trailhead. A Northwest Forest Pass or interagency pass is required to park, plus a free self-issued Alp

pins.name: Esmeralda Basin Trailhead (North Fork Teanaway Rd)
Esmeralda Basin Trailhead (North Fork Teanaway Rd)
Esmeralda Basin Trailhead (North Fork Teanaway Rd)
Esmeralda Basin / Ingalls Lake Trailhead (North Fork Teanaway Rd, FR 9737)

text: Drive the North Fork Teanaway Road (FR-9737) to its end, where the Esmeralda Basin Trailhead — also known as the Lake Ingalls trailhead — sits at about 4,270 ft. The Ingalls Way Trail starts here and climbs toward Ingalls Pass and Ingalls Lake. This is the Teanaway side of Stuart, so make sure it is the lot you want: the North Ridge routes on this mountain are also reached from the opposite Mounta

pins.name: Esmeralda Basin / Ingalls Way Trailhead (North Fork Teanaway Rd, FR-9737) via Longs Pass

text: Drive the North Fork Teanaway Road and Forest Road 9737 to the road end at the Esmeralda trailhead, about 4,250 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park; fill out the free wilderness permit at the trailhead.

From I-90 Exit 85, take SR 970 east about 7 miles and turn left onto Teanaway Road. Follow it north as it becomes the North Fork Teanaway Road to the end of pavement at 29 Pines Campground, then continue straight on gravel FR 9737 for about 10 miles to its end at the Esmeralda Basin and Ingalls Lake trailhead, about a mile past the De Roux campground. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park.

pins.name: Esmeralda Basin / Ingalls Lake Trailhead (N Fork Teanaway River Rd)

text: Drive the North Fork Teanaway River Road (FS-9737) to its end at the Esmeralda Basin / Longs Pass trailhead, about 4,300 ft. The road is usually open to the trailhead by early June, but the route itself wants late June through September, once the Longs Pass approach and the rock are snow-free. From the lot take the Longs Pass Trail (#1229), which climbs roughly 2.3 miles and 2,300 ft to Longs Pass

From Cle Elum, head northeast on SR-970 about 5 miles, turn onto the Teanaway River Road and follow it roughly 23 miles to the road end. The small lot fills fast on summer weekends — a Northwest Forest Pass is required and there is a self-issue wilderness permit at the kiosk.

From I-90 Exit 52 (Snoqualmie Pass West), turn north under the freeway onto Alpental Road and follow it about 1.3 miles to the road end at the Alpental ski area lot, the Snow Lake trailhead parking, at about 3,100 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required. The side roads named Strasse are private and closed to climbers, on foot as well as by car.

pins.name: Alpental parking lot / Snow Lake TH #1013
Alpental parking lot / Snow Lake TH #1013
Alpental parking lot / Snow Lake TH #1013

text: Take I-90 to Exit 52 at Snoqualmie Pass and follow Alpental Road to its end, parking in the upper Alpental lot at about 3,100 feet. The Snow Lake Trail #1013 starts here; a cat track leaves the end of the lot and runs up the valley just left of the stream. Plan an alpine start, since this route is normally done car-to-car in one long day.

pins.name: Alpental Ski Area Trailhead (Snow Lake Trail #1013)

text: From I-90 Exit 52 at Snoqualmie Pass, go north under the freeway and take the second right onto Alpental Road, then drive about 1.3 miles to the Alpental Ski Area lot; the Snow Lake trailhead is at the north end of the day-use lot. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park, and a free self-issue wilderness permit is filled out at the trailhead.

pins.name: Alpental Ski Area parking lot / Snow Lake Trailhead
Alpental / Snow Lake Trailhead Parking Lot
Alpental Ski Area / Snow Lake Trailhead parking lot

text: From I-90 take Exit 52 (Snoqualmie Pass West) and turn left (north), passing under the freeway. Take the second right onto Alpental Road and drive about 1.3 miles to its end at the Alpental Ski Area parking lot, at about 3,100 ft, where the Snow Lake Trail #1013 starts. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park, and a free self-issue wilderness permit is required.
From I-90 Exit 52 at Snoqualmie Pass, follow Alpental Road to its end, staying past the lower ski-area lots to the upper parking area.

From US 97 between Leavenworth and Blewett Pass, about 7 miles south of the US 2 junction (near milepost 178), turn west onto Ingalls Creek Road. Cross Peshastin Creek, bear left, and drive to the trailhead at the road's end, about 1,900 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass or Interagency pass is required to park; fill out the free self-issued wilderness permit at the trailhead.

From US 101 north of Shelton, turn west on West Skokomish Valley Road, follow it about 5.6 miles and continue uphill onto Forest Road 23. Stay on FS 23, keeping left at intersections, then turn right onto FS 2361 and drive about 5 miles to the road end at about 1,100 ft. FS 2361 is rough and potholed and is closed to vehicles October 1 to April 30.

From I-90 Exit 32 (436th Ave SE), turn north over the freeway and drive 0.5 mile to SE North Bend Way. Turn left, and in 0.25 mile turn right onto SE Mount Si Road. In 2.9 miles, past the Little Si and Mount Si trailheads, the paved Mount Teneriffe Trailhead lot is on the left. A Discover Pass is required to park.
From I-90 Exit 32, go north on 436th Ave SE to SE North Bend Way and turn left; after 0.3 mi turn right on SE Mount Si Road and drive 2.4 mi to the lot on the left.
Descend Mount Ellinor's standard trail through the subalpine slopes and forest to the upper trailhead at about 3,500 ft, where the shuttle car should be waiting.

From US-101 at Hoodsport, take SR 119 (Lake Cushman Road) 9.3 miles to its end, turn right on FS Road 24 for 1.6 miles, then left on FS Road 2419 for 4.9 miles to the lower trailhead. Continue 1.7 miles farther and turn left on FS Road 2419-014 to the upper trailhead lot at its end, about 3,500 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required.

pins.name: Staircase Ranger Station / North Fork Skokomish Trailhead
Staircase Trailhead (North Fork Skokomish, Olympic NP)
Staircase Ranger Station / North Fork Skokomish Trailhead

text: From US 101 in Hoodsport, follow SR 119 (Lake Cushman Road) about 9 miles to a T-intersection, turn left and continue about 5.4 miles on what becomes FR 24, then turn right into Olympic National Park and drive about 1.2 miles to the Staircase Ranger Station and its large trailhead parking area. The last miles are gravel. A national park entrance pass is required.

pins.name: Staircase Ranger Station / North Fork Skokomish Trailhead

text: From US 101 at Hoodsport, turn west onto SR 119 (Lake Cushman Road) and drive just over 9 miles to its T-junction with FR 24, then turn left. The pavement ends after 1.7 miles; continue 3.7 miles on gravel to a junction, turn right, and drive 1.2 miles to the Staircase Ranger Station, with trailhead parking across from the campground. An Olympic National Park entrance fee applies.

pins.name: Dingford Creek / Middle Fork Snoqualmie Trailhead

text: From I-90 Exit 34, go north on 468th Ave SE about 0.6 mile and turn right onto the Middle Fork Snoqualmie Road (FS Road 56). Follow it about 12 miles to the main Middle Fork trailhead, cross the large concrete bridge, and turn right onto the gravel road signed for Dingford and Dutch Miller Gap. Drive this heavily potholed road about 6 miles to the parking area at the gate, at about 1,650 ft.
FR-56 up the Middle Fork Snoqualmie to the lot is heavily potholed and rutted; parties in low-clearance cars routinely park short and walk the last stretch, which adds to an already long day.

pins.name: Dingford Creek Trailhead (Dutch Miller Gap Trail)

text: From I-90 Exit 34, go north on 468th Ave SE about 0.6 mile and turn right onto the Middle Fork Road (FS Road 56). Follow it about 12 miles as the pavement gives out, pass the Middle Fork Trailhead, and bear right onto the rough road signed for Dingford and Dutch Miller Gap. Drive about 5 to 6 more rough miles, high clearance recommended, to the gate at the Dingford Creek Trailhead at about 1,500 f

From the T-intersection at the end of North Lake Cushman Road, turn right onto FS Road 24 and continue about 1.5 miles, then turn left onto FS Road 2419 and follow it up the Big Creek drainage for roughly 6.6 miles to its end at a small trailhead and parking area near 3,026 ft. Display a Northwest Forest Pass; no wilderness permit is needed.

pins.name: Unsigned climbers' path off FS Road 56

text: From North Bend take I-90 exit 34 and follow 468th Ave SE north about 0.6 mile to the Middle Fork Snoqualmie River Road (FS Road 56). Continue roughly 16 miles up FS 56, which bends right around the 12-mile mark; the upper miles are rough gravel and dirt, and high clearance is recommended. You are aiming for an unsigned, easy-to-miss climbers' and fishermen's path on the north shoulder of the road

From US-2 at the western edge of Leavenworth, turn onto Icicle Creek Road and drive 8.4 miles, then turn left onto Eightmile Road (FS Road 7601) and stay on the rough dirt road for 3.7 miles to reach the Stuart Lake Trailhead at about 3,400 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park and overnight trips May 15 to Oct 31 need an Enchantment permit; the road is usually gated November into May.

From US-2 at the west edge of Leavenworth, turn onto Icicle Creek Road and drive about 8.4 miles, then turn left onto FS Road 7601 (Eightmile Road) and follow the potholed gravel road about 3.7 miles to its end at the Stuart Lake Trailhead. A Northwest Forest Pass is required; day visitors self-issue a free Enchantment permit at the trailhead, and overnight stays need a lottery permit. FS Road 760

From US 2 at the west edge of Leavenworth, turn onto Icicle Creek Road and drive about 8.4 miles, then turn left onto FR 7601 and follow the bumpy gravel road about 3.7 miles to the Stuart Lake Trailhead at its end. FR 7601 is normally closed in winter. A Northwest Forest Pass is required, and a day-use Enchantment permit is self-issued at the trailhead.

From US 2 at the west end of Leavenworth, take Icicle Creek Road 8.5 miles and turn left onto FS Road 7601 (Eightmile Road). Follow this bumpy dirt road about 4 miles to the road end. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park, the road is closed in winter, and day trips need the free self-issued Enchantment day-use permit at the trailhead.

From US-2 at the western edge of Leavenworth, turn onto Icicle Creek Road and drive 8.4 miles, then turn left onto Eightmile Road (FS Road 7601) and follow the rough dirt road 3.7 miles to the Stuart Lake Trailhead at about 3,400 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park and day trips need the free self-issued Enchantment day-use permit; the road is usually gated November into May.
